working_tree_note: Parent coordinated RAM-only provenance/profile metadata and a harmless service_probe source after this baseline; this report does not approve a new executable revision.

environment.bwrap: not installed; not required by this proposal

existing_gaps.finding: profile/path checks, global-lock preparation, source hashing, output/file/canary provisioning and launch.json writing currently run outside the unit; the recorded start time follows provisioning.
observer, final source/canary/archive hashes, allocation checks, log parsing and result.json writing run outside payload CPU/RAM accounting; elapsed is sampled before final work.
Formal BUILD_ONLY is correctly fail-closed. RAM approval alone must not remove these guards.

preferred_design.topology: One outer systemd user service, not a second sibling transient service. ExecStartPre provisioner, ExecStart controller and ordinary fork/exec worker descendants share the same aggregate parent cgroup. No user business controller or observer remains in the host.

host_launcher.allowed: Fixed exec-only systemd activation request with bounded literal arguments; no package imports, source hashing, UUID/file provisioning, archive readback, protocol parsing, scientific checks, resource decisions or result writing.
host_launcher.boundary: The generic activation client and systemd/kernel control plane remain an explicit infrastructure boundary. Their existence must be disclosed; this is not a claim about whole-machine CPU/RAM. If the requested contract includes that client itself, independently hard-bound/account it in the same total budget or keep FULL false; do not silently exempt a user controller.
host_launcher.observer: Move the functional observer inside. An outside terminal/status display may not enforce limits or compute acceptance/results. A custom external Python postprocessor is not a replacement for enclosed finalization.

preprovision.method: Exactly one reviewed ExecStartPre helper runs after the service cgroup resource limits are active. It creates only fresh fixed-count empty transport/metadata files and the fixed canary/lock records; refuses existing outputs, symlinks, hardlinks and unexpected ownership. It performs any source/config preparation hashes inside this same envelope.
preprovision.manager_handoff: Upstream v255 gives OpenFile descriptors to ExecStart (EXEC_PASS_FDS), not ExecStartPre. Therefore create fixed files inside ExecStartPre, then have the manager open them for the main controller. Use no graceful opening and require exact FD count/names/dev/inode/access in the controller.
preprovision.stdio: Use StandardOutput/StandardError=null for preparation, or another explicitly bounded manager-native transport. Do not reference not-yet-created output parents for preparation stdio. The main controller duplicates verified named protocol/log FDs to1/2.
preprovision.mount_lifetime: ExecStartPre and ExecStart receive separate mount namespaces; a private tmpfs created for Pre does not carry its contents into Main. Only fixed host transport files may carry preparation state. Main must independently attest its work/tmp tmpfs quotas and readonly source.
preprovision.disk_gate: BLOCKED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED: do not grant a general writable host output directory and call it an aggregate disk limit. Before the first creation, require an actually enforced quota/bounded backing filesystem OR a separately reviewed finite inode/FD factory that cannot create an unbounded number of files/directories or allocate data/extents. RLIMIT_FSIZE and a later allocated-byte check alone are insufficient. The existing seccomp allocation guard, fixed FD count and read-only post-factory host view must cover the actual early preparation window, not only later business callbacks.

main_controller.scope: Profile/source/Git preflight, worker launch, monitoring, source preservation checks, archive streaming/readback/hashes, receipt writing, postflight and normal cleanup all execute under the outer cgroup/namespace; source is readonly; host writes use only verified fixed descriptors.
main_controller.worker_launch: Ordinary Popen/fork/exec within the same service. Calling the old backend.run_job/systemd-run here would launch a sibling cgroup and would NOT close the gap.
main_controller.counters: Read the aggregate parent cpu.stat/memory.peak/events/pids files locally; remove dependence on the hidden user D-Bus socket. Check every helper belongs to the same accounting ancestor.
main_controller.job_count: Single-job protection must precede Pre provisioning and persist through final receipt/cleanup. A flock first acquired in Main does not cover Pre. Prefer one fixed fail-if-existing transient unit identity, or independently verified retained-lock FD handoff; do not assume a Pre lock survives process exit.

termination_and_receipts.normal: Controller reaps/kills worker descendants using stable PID identities/process groups and checks no non-controller workload PIDs remain. Do not write cgroup.kill for the controller own group and then expect it to produce a receipt.
termination_and_receipts.controller_loss: Manager RuntimeMax/OOMPolicy/KillMode enforce termination even if controller dies. Preserve partial evidence. Missing complete finalization is FAIL/BLOCKED, never an automatic PASS.
termination_and_receipts.stop_post: If used, one bounded ExecStopPost helper executes inside the same accounting ancestor. Count every start/control/stop phase in the wall and CPU upper bound. Its namespace is fresh: read only persistent fixed transports, not vanished Main tmpfs data. It may record failure, not resume work/retry or transform a failure into success.
termination_and_receipts.final_accounting: Do not call a pre-final-write cpu.stat measurement the final whole-job count. Record its phase explicitly and use authoritative cached manager final counters for later independent status readback. Do not run an unenclosed custom archive/hash/result workflow after the unit; if that observer is required for acceptance, it must itself be enclosed/accounted. Whole-cgroup empty is checked after the final controller/collector exits, rather than pretending the still-running collector makes populated=0.

budgets.RAM: User approved aggregate512MiB/swap0 for harmless tests, future proposed aggregate2GiB/swap0. Limits cover controller+workers+all helpers+charged tmpfs/page cache together; not512MiB per process or unit.
budgets.CPU: Keep aggregate4s fixture /14400s future. Require actual zero burst and fixed single CPU affinity. CPU quota times a fully enumerated worst-case lifecycle duration plus one-period allowance must fit the aggregate cap; cumulative watchdog is extra protection.
budgets.wall: Keep13s fixture /14400s future. RuntimeMax alone excludes preparation and stop-post. TimeoutStart may apply to each Pre/Main phase and TimeoutStop to multiple stop transitions. Adding Pre while retaining a naive start+run+stop formula is not valid; repartition internal phase budgets or remain BLOCKED without increasing aggregate ceilings.
budgets.disk: Keep16MiB fixture /5GiB future and all per-file limits. Include both actual tmpfs quotas, rounded allocated host blocks, all preprovisioned files/directories, metadata/canary/global mutex and fixed source/control reserve. No sparse/fallocate/xattr/io_uring escape; no quota assumption from a filesystem name alone.

required_environment_feature_probe.scope: One fixed harmless non-stress service only, no MG5/model/HH native executable. Parent coordinates exact source/command and preserves actual failure.
features: User-service cgroup limits are effective before Pre and Main code.
PrivateUsers plus readonly source and two independent quota-sized tmpfs mounts are supported.
ExecStartPre fixed empty file -> ExecStart strict OpenFile named FD sequence works on installed255.4.
Pre and Main share the expected aggregate accounting ancestor while private mount contents are not incorrectly assumed shared.
Output provisioning/fixed inode bounds or actual quota are established before stress acceptance, not inferred from a /usr/bin/true probe.
required_environment_feature_probe.stop_rule: On any compatibility failure stop and preserve it. Do not install tools, expand privileges, remove protections, enlarge limits, or claim the environment is inherently incapable from a single setup failure.

validation_before_any_FULL_claim: Actual positive normal whole-controller workflow, including final receipt/archive readback and final cleanup.
CPU/RAM/wall/disk/abnormal injection in actual Pre provisioning, controller preflight, child, observer, hashing/readback, receipt, postflight and failure-finalization phases.

Aggregate controller+child memory/CPU cases; controller death; orphan/setsid descendants; final collector failure; sparse extent/xattr/io_uring bypass rejection; simultaneous-job refusal before provisioning.
Independent final numerical/data review must reject missing counters, wrong membership, partial receipts and residual processes.
Current47 payload fixtures may remain useful regression evidence but cannot alone certify the newly defined complete controller.

primary_references.used_for: Cgroup realization and conditional descriptor passing in service spawning.
Start-pre uses sandbox/control flags without EXEC_PASS_FDS.
OpenFile access modes; separate command mount namespaces; RuntimeMax/start/stop semantics; memory/swap and CPU quota policy.

next_step: Parent may execute only the separately reviewed fixed non-stress compatibility probe under the user RAM approval. A successful /usr/bin/true or namespace probe is not full resource validation. Review a concrete implementation and new exact source before new complete-controller stress tests. Formal BUILD/native/ME/integrals/events stay forbidden.
